_comment: Curated set of notable LIGO/Virgo binary-black-hole (BBH) merger events from GWTC (the Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog). IMPORTANT: real gravitational-wave sky localizations are irregular, often banana- or ring-shaped regions spanning tens to hundreds of square degrees, not points. The ra/dec given here are illustrative centroids only, placed inside the published 90%-credible region for map display purposes -- they are NOT precise sky positions. Every entry is marked approx:true for this reason and localization_area_deg2 gives the rough published 90% credible-region size.

events.name: GW150914
events.notes: First direct detection of gravitational waves and of a binary black hole merger. Detected by the two LIGO detectors only, giving a long ring/annulus-shaped localization; the centroid shown is illustrative.

events.name: GW151226
events.notes: Nicknamed the 'Boxing Day event'. Two-detector localization spanning a very large area of sky; centroid is illustrative only.

events.name: GW170104
events.notes: Confirmed BBH population properties consistent with GW150914; broad, poorly-constrained localization.

events.name: GW170608
events.notes: Lowest-mass binary black hole merger reported in GWTC-1, bridging toward neutron-star mass scales.
events.source: Abbott et al. 2017, ApJL 851, L35 (LIGO/Virgo GWTC-1)

events.name: GW170814
events.notes: First BBH merger observed by three detectors (two LIGO + Virgo), dramatically shrinking the localization region compared to two-detector events; also allowed the first tests of gravitational-wave polarization.

events.name: GW190521
events.notes: Merger remnant of ~142 solar masses is the first robust intermediate-mass black hole detected by any means; progenitor masses fall partly in the 'pair-instability mass gap', suggesting a hierarchical (black-hole-merger-product) formation channel.
events.source: Abbott et al. 2020, PRL 125, 101102 and ApJL 900, L13 (LIGO/Virgo GWTC-2)
